definition_en: a round solid shape, an area of activity, or a group within society
core_image: 地球仪在灯下缓缓转动，蓝色球面上映出窗外的光
scene: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
sceneCN: 这里 sphere 是「球体」（第 1 个义项）；句意：地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。

senses.title: A round solid
senses.definition: a perfectly round solid shape like a ball
senses.definitionCN: 像球一样完全圆形的立体形状
senses.example: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。
senses.why: This is the geometric sense at the root of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词根源处的几何含义。

senses.title: An area of activity
senses.definition: a particular area of activity or knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 活动或知识的某一特定范围
senses.example: She works in the sphere of education.
senses.exampleCN: 她在教育领域工作。
senses.why: A sphere encloses a space, and so does an area of work.
senses.whyCN: 球体围出一片空间，工作领域也是如此。

senses.title: A social circle
senses.definition: a group of people with shared interests or position
senses.definitionCN: 兴趣或地位相同的一群人
senses.example: He moved in a different social sphere.
senses.exampleCN: 他进入了另一个社交圈子。
senses.why: A social circle is a sphere drawn around people.
senses.whyCN: 社交圈就是围绕人们画出的一个球。

intro.en: Sphere came from Greek sphaira, a ball, through Latin.
intro.cn: sphere 从希腊语 sphaira（球）经拉丁语而来。

items.en: Sphaira meant a ball or a globe.
items.cn: sphaira 意为球或球体。

items.en: Sphaera named a globe and the heavens.
items.cn: sphaera 指球体与天球。

items.en: Sphere entered English as the shape of the heavens.
items.cn: sphere 以天球的形状之义进入英语。

items.en: It named the earth and other round bodies.
items.cn: 它指地球等圆形天体。

items.en: It came to mean a field of activity or influence.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示活动或影响力的范围。

note.en: Sphere is compared with look-alike words and words for round shapes and fields.
note.cn: 把 sphere 与形近词以及表示圆形和领域的词作比较。

entries.definition: a round model of the earth
an area of study or work

normalIntro.en: A sphere is a space drawn into a perfect round, then borrowed for any enclosed area.
normalIntro.cn: sphere 是一片被画成完美圆形的空间，随后借指任何被围起来的范围。

normal.en: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
normal.cn: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。

normal.en: She works in the sphere of education.
He moved in a different social sphere.
normal.cn: 他进入了另一个社交圈子。

normal.en: The moon appears as a pale sphere.
normal.cn: 月亮看上去是一个苍白的球体。

normal.en: Each country guards its sphere of influence.
normal.cn: 每个国家都守护自己的势力范围。

abstract.en: A sphere is a wall that has no corners.
abstract.cn: 球体是一堵没有角落的墙。

abstract.en: Every field is a sphere someone drew around an interest.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都是某人围绕兴趣画出的球。

abstract.en: The wider your sphere, the more edges you meet.
abstract.cn: 圈子越大，你碰到的边界越多。

examples.en: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.
examples.cn: 地球仪是一个代表地球的球体。

examples.en: She works in the sphere of education.
examples.cn: 她在教育领域工作。

examples.en: He moved in a different social sphere.
examples.cn: 他进入了另一个社交圈子。

dict_mnemonic.text: sphere 源自希腊语 sphaira（球），指「球体」，引申为「范围、领域、圈子」；spherical 是「球形的」，hemisphere 是「半球」，sphere of influence 是「势力范围」。

root: 来自希腊语 sphaira（球），经拉丁语 sphaera 进入英语，核心义为球体，引申为像球一样围出的范围、领域与社交圈。

sensesIntro.en: Sphere means a round solid, an area of activity, or a social circle.
sensesIntro.cn: sphere 指球体、活动领域，或社交圈子。

core.en: A space enclosed in a perfect round.
core.cn: 被完美圆形围起的空间。

branches.en: A globe turns under a lamp.
branches.cn: 地球仪在灯下转动。

branches.en: A teacher works inside one branch of knowledge.
branches.cn: 一位教师在某一知识分支内工作。

branches.en: Guests gather in a small circle of friends.
branches.cn: 宾客聚成一个小小的朋友圈。

branches.en: A round boundary and a bounded field share one shape.
branches.cn: 圆形边界与有界的领域共享一种形状。

branches.en: Work and society each draw their own circles.
branches.cn: 工作与社会各自画出自己的圆圈。

intro.en: Sphere forms adjectives and compound worlds.
intro.cn: sphere 构成形容词和表示各种圈层的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Greek sphaira through Latin sphaera, a ball.
latinIntro.cn: 其词根是希腊语 sphaira，经拉丁语 sphaera（球）而来。

items.example: A globe is a sphere that represents the earth.

items.example: The lamps hung like small spheres.

items.exampleCN: 这些种子几乎是球形的。

items.example: The northern hemisphere is colder now.

items.exampleCN: 大气层保护着这颗行星。

items.meaning: the living zone of the earth

definition_en: a strong-flavoured substance from a plant used in cooking, or something that adds interest
core_image: 研钵里堆着肉桂、丁香和胡椒，木杵一压，香气散开
scene: 肉桂为热苹果酒增添香气。Cinnamon adds spice to the hot cider.
sceneCN: 这里 spice 是「香料」（第 1 个义项）；句意：肉桂为热苹果酒增添香气。

senses.title: A cooking flavouring
senses.definition: a substance from a plant used to flavour food
senses.definitionCN: 来自植物、用于给食物调味的物质
senses.example: Cinnamon adds spice to the hot cider.
senses.exampleCN: 肉桂为热苹果酒增添香气。
senses.why: This is the central kitchen sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词核心的厨房含义。

senses.title: Something exciting
senses.definition: an extra quality that makes something more interesting or exciting
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物更有趣或更刺激的额外特质
senses.example: A little danger adds spice to the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 一点危险给旅行增添了刺激。
senses.why: Flavour in food became flavour in experience.
senses.whyCN: 食物中的味道变成了经历中的趣味。

senses.title: To flavour
senses.definition: to add spice to food, or to make something more interesting
senses.definitionCN: 给食物加香料，或使某事物更有趣
senses.example: She spiced the soup with pepper.
senses.exampleCN: 她往汤里加了胡椒调味。
senses.why: The noun turned into the action of adding flavour.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为添加风味的动作。

intro.en: Spice came from Latin species, goods or kinds, through Old French.
intro.cn: spice 从拉丁语 species（货物、种类）经古法语而来。

items.en: Species meant kind, appearance, or goods.
items.cn: species 意为种类、外观或货物。

items.en: Espice named valuable aromatic goods.
items.cn: espice 指珍贵的芳香货物。

items.en: Spice entered English as an aromatic plant product.
items.cn: spice 以芳香植物制品之义进入英语。

items.en: The spice trade made it a word of wealth.
items.cn: 香料贸易使它成为代表财富的词。

items.en: It came to mean anything that adds interest.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示任何增添趣味的事物。

note.en: Spice is compared with look-alike words and words for flavourings.
note.cn: 把 spice 与形近词以及表示调味品的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spice is flavour strong enough to wake a dish up.
normalIntro.cn: spice 是足以把一道菜唤醒的浓烈风味。

normal.en: Cinnamon adds spice to the hot cider.
normal.cn: 肉桂为热苹果酒增添香气。

normal.en: A little danger adds spice to the trip.
normal.cn: 一点危险给旅行增添了刺激。

normal.en: She spiced the soup with pepper.
normal.cn: 她往汤里加了胡椒调味。

normal.en: The market sells mixed spices in paper bags.
normal.cn: 市场上用纸袋出售混合香料。

normal.en: The spice trade once moved empires.
normal.cn: 香料贸易曾推动帝国的兴衰。

abstract.en: Spice is a small amount that changes everything.
abstract.cn: 香料是能改变一切的小分量。

abstract.en: A life without spice is a meal without salt.
abstract.cn: 没有情趣的生活，是一顿没有盐的饭。

abstract.en: The rarest flavour was once worth more than gold.
abstract.cn: 最稀有的味道，曾比黄金更贵。

examples.en: Cinnamon adds spice to the hot cider.
examples.cn: 肉桂为热苹果酒增添香气。

examples.en: A little danger adds spice to the trip.
examples.cn: 一点危险给旅行增添了刺激。

examples.en: She spiced the soup with pepper.
examples.cn: 她往汤里加了胡椒调味。

dict_mnemonic.text: spice 源自拉丁语 species（货物、种类），本指珍贵香料，后引申为「情趣」；spicy 是「辛辣的、有情趣的」，spice up 是「增添情趣」，spice trade 是「香料贸易」。

root: 来自拉丁语 species（种类、货物），经古法语 espice 进入英语，本指各类珍贵芳香货物，后专指香料，引申为情趣与刺激。

sensesIntro.en: Spice means a flavouring from plants, something that adds excitement, or to flavour.
sensesIntro.cn: spice 指植物香料、增添情趣之物，或加香料。

core.en: A small strong thing that transforms a whole.
core.cn: 能改变整体的小而浓烈之物。

branches.en: Cinnamon scents a pot of cider.
branches.cn: 肉桂为锅里的苹果酒添香。

branches.en: A hint of danger sharpens a journey.
branches.cn: 一丝危险让旅程更鲜明。

branches.en: A cook shakes pepper into soup.
branches.cn: 厨师往汤里抖入胡椒。

branches.en: Flavour in food and excitement in life are the same image.
branches.cn: 食物的味道与生活的刺激是同一个意象。

branches.en: The substance and the act of adding it share one word.
branches.cn: 香料与添加香料的行为共用一个词。

intro.en: Spice forms adjectives and nouns of flavour.
intro.cn: spice 构成表示风味的形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is species, kind or goods, which also gave special and specify.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 species（种类、货物），也衍生出 special 和 specify。

items.example: Cinnamon adds spice to the hot cider.

items.example: The market sells mixed spices in paper bags.
items.exampleCN: 市场上用纸袋出售混合香料。

items.example: The curry is too spicy for me.
items.exampleCN: 这道咖喱对我来说太辣了。

items.example: He likes the spiciness of the sauce.

items.meaning: a place or stock of spices
items.example: The old spicery smelled of cloves.
items.exampleCN: 老香料店散发着丁香的气味。

definition_zh: 蜘蛛；蛛网状物；网络爬虫
definition_en: a small eight-legged creature that spins webs
core_image: 一只蜘蛛在窗角的网中央静候
scene: 蜘蛛在墙角织了一张网。A spider built a web in the corner.
sceneCN: 这里 spider 是「蜘蛛」（第 1 个义项）；句意：蜘蛛在墙角织了一张网。

senses.title: The web-spinning animal
senses.definition: a small creature with eight legs that spins webs
senses.definitionCN: 一种八条腿、会结网的小生物
senses.example: A spider hung from the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蜘蛛从天花板上垂下来。
senses.why: This is the everyday animal sense.
senses.whyCN: 最日常的动物义，是这个词的核心。

senses.title: Thin network shape
senses.definition: something thin and network-like
senses.definitionCN: 细长而呈网状的事物
senses.example: Fine spidery lines covered the old map.
senses.exampleCN: 旧地图上布满细如蛛丝的线条。
senses.why: The shape of a web is borrowed for thin networks.
senses.whyCN: 由蛛网的形状引申到细密的网状线条。

senses.title: A web-crawling program
senses.definition: a program that crawls the web and collects pages
senses.definitionCN: 在网络上爬行并抓取网页的程序
senses.example: The spider indexed the new pages overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 网络爬虫一夜之间索引了新页面。
senses.why: Search engines borrow the web image for crawling.
senses.whyCN: 搜索引擎借蜘蛛结网来比喻抓取网页。

intro.en: Spider is an old English word built from the idea of spinning.
intro.cn: spider 是古英语词，构词理据与「纺」有关。

items.en: Spiþra named the web-spinning creature.
items.cn: spiþra 指结网的生物。

items.en: The form settled as spither and then spider.
items.cn: 词形先作 spither，后定为 spider。

items.en: The word stayed the everyday name of the animal.
items.cn: 这个词一直是这种动物的日常名称。

items.en: The web shape gave a sense for thin networks.
items.cn: 蛛网的形状引申出细网之义。

items.en: Computing borrowed it for web-crawling programs.
items.cn: 计算机领域借它指网页抓取程序。

note.en: Spider is compared with look-alike words and words for small creatures.
note.cn: 把 spider 与形近词以及表示小生物的词语作比较。

entries.definition: a net spun by a spider

normalIntro.en: A spider is a small weaver with eight legs.
normalIntro.cn: 蜘蛛就是有八条腿的小织工。

normal.en: A spider is on the wall.
A spider ran across the floor.

abstract.en: The spider works in the dark and waits for light.
abstract.cn: 蜘蛛在暗处织网，等天亮。

abstract.en: A web is patience made visible.
abstract.cn: 蛛网，是看得见的耐心。

abstract.en: Small legs can hold a whole corner.
abstract.cn: 小小的腿，也能守住整个角落。

examples.en: A spider hung from the ceiling.
examples.cn: 一只蜘蛛从天花板上垂下来。

examples.en: Fine spidery lines covered the old map.
examples.cn: 旧地图上布满细如蛛丝的线条。

examples.en: The spider indexed the new pages overnight.
examples.cn: 网络爬虫一夜之间索引了新页面。

dict_mnemonic.text: spider 与 spin（纺、旋转）同源，结网就是「纺」；spider web 是蜘蛛网，spider sense 是「蜘蛛直觉」；注意与 spill、spin 区分。

root: 来自古英语 spīþra，与 spin（纺线）同源，核心义是「结网的生物」，后由网状形状引申到细网与网络爬虫。

sensesIntro.en: Spider means the web-spinning animal, a thin network shape, or a web-crawling program.
sensesIntro.cn: spider 指结网的蜘蛛、细长的网状物，或抓取网页的爬虫程序。

core.en: A small weaver that waits in its own net.
core.cn: 守在自己网里的小织工。

branches.en: Eight legs grip the wall.
branches.cn: 八条腿抓住墙壁。

branches.en: Silk is drawn out and crossed.
branches.cn: 丝被拉出、交错。

branches.en: Thin lines spread like a net.
branches.cn: 细线像网一样铺开。

branches.en: The animal and the net share one shape.
branches.cn: 动物与网，共用一种形状。

branches.en: The net becomes a tool for catching pages.
branches.cn: 网变成抓取网页的工具。

intro.en: Spider forms plurals, adjectives, and compounds.
intro.cn: spider 构成复数、形容词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Spider has no Latin root; it comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: spider 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语。

definition_en: to let liquid fall out of a container
core_image: 打翻的水杯在桌面淌开一片水痕
scene: 她把咖啡洒在了桌上。She spilled coffee on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 spill 是「洒出」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把咖啡洒在了桌上。

senses.title: Knock liquid over
senses.definition: to cause liquid to flow out by accident
senses.definitionCN: 不小心使液体流出来
senses.example: She spilled coffee on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她把咖啡洒在了桌上。
senses.why: This is the everyday accident sense.
senses.whyCN: 最常见的意外用法，指不慎弄洒。

senses.title: Flow over the edge
senses.definition: to flow over the edge of a container
senses.definitionCN: 从容器边缘漫出来
senses.example: The river spilled over its banks.
senses.exampleCN: 河水漫过了河岸。
senses.why: The liquid moves beyond its limit.
senses.whyCN: 液体超出了容器的边界。

senses.title: Let a secret out
senses.definition: to reveal secret information
senses.definitionCN: 把秘密信息说出去
senses.example: He spilled the whole plan to a reporter.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整个计划泄露给了记者。
senses.why: Words are pictured as liquid escaping.
senses.whyCN: 把话语比作流出来的液体。

intro.en: Spill is an Old English verb meaning to destroy or waste.
intro.cn: spill 是古英语动词，原意为毁坏或浪费。

items.en: Spillan meant to destroy or shed blood.
items.cn: spillan 意为毁坏或使流血。

items.en: The sense narrowed to letting liquid fall.
items.cn: 词义缩小为让液体落下。

items.en: Spill out and spill over described overflowing.
items.cn: spill out 与 spill over 表示溢出。

items.en: Spill the beans became a phrase for telling secrets.
items.cn: spill the beans 成为泄露秘密的说法。

items.en: Oil spill named a large accidental leak.
items.cn: oil spill 指大规模意外泄漏。

note.en: Spill is compared with look-alike words and words for liquid movement.
note.cn: 把 spill 与形近词以及表示液体流动的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spill is liquid losing its cup.
normalIntro.cn: spill 就是液体失去了杯子。

abstract.en: What spills cannot be poured back.
abstract.cn: 洒出去的，倒不回去。

abstract.en: A secret is a liquid too.
abstract.cn: 秘密也是一种液体。

abstract.en: The floor remembers every spill.
abstract.cn: 地板记得每一次打翻。

examples.en: She spilled coffee on the table.
examples.cn: 她把咖啡洒在了桌上。

examples.en: The river spilled over its banks.
examples.cn: 河水漫过了河岸。

examples.en: He spilled the whole plan to a reporter.
examples.cn: 他把整个计划泄露给了记者。

dict_mnemonic.text: spill 是「洒、溢出」，spill the beans 是「泄露秘密」，oil spill 是「石油泄漏」；注意与 spell（拼写）、spoil（破坏）区分。

sensesIntro.en: Spill means to knock liquid over, to flow past the edge, or to let a secret out.
sensesIntro.cn: spill 指弄洒液体、从边缘溢出，或泄露秘密。

core.en: Liquid escaping its container.
core.cn: 液体逃出了容器。

branches.en: A hand knocks the cup.
branches.cn: 一只手碰翻了杯子。

branches.en: Water climbs the rim and crosses it.
branches.cn: 水爬过杯沿，越了出去。

branches.en: A whispered word reaches the wrong ear.
branches.cn: 一句低语传进了不该听的耳朵。

branches.en: Accident and overflow share one motion.
branches.cn: 打翻与溢出，是同一种流动。

branches.en: Both water and news go where they should not.
branches.cn: 水和消息，都会流到不该去的地方。

intro.en: Spill has verb forms and compounds.
intro.cn: spill 有动词变化形式和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Spill has no Latin root; it comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: spill 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语。

items.example: The ink was spilt on the desk.
The bag is spilling its contents.
items.exampleCN: 袋子里的东西正撒出来。
溢出效应影响了附近城镇。

definition_en: to turn round quickly, to make thread, or to invent a story
core_image: 陀螺在地面上飞快旋转
scene: 孩子们看着陀螺旋转。The children watched the top spin.
sceneCN: 这里 spin 是「旋转」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们看着陀螺旋转。

senses.title: Turn round fast
senses.definition: to turn round quickly and repeatedly
senses.definitionCN: 快速地一圈圈转动
senses.example: The wheel spun faster and faster.
senses.exampleCN: 轮子越转越快。
senses.why: The core physical sense is rapid turning.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的物理义，指快速打转。

senses.title: Draw out thread
senses.definition: to make thread from wool or cotton
senses.definitionCN: 把羊毛或棉花纺成线
senses.example: She spun wool into thread.
senses.exampleCN: 她把羊毛纺成了线。
senses.why: The old craft sense is the historical source.
senses.whyCN: 古老的手工业义，是这个词的历史来源。

senses.title: Invent a tale
senses.definition: to invent a story or an explanation
senses.definitionCN: 编造故事或说法
senses.example: He spun a tale about a lost city.
senses.exampleCN: 他编了一个关于失落之城的故事。
senses.why: Threads of words are pictured as being drawn out.
senses.whyCN: 把话语比作一根根抽出来的线。

intro.en: Spin is an Old English verb for drawing out thread.
intro.cn: spin 是古英语动词，指把纤维抽成线。

items.en: Spinnan meant to draw out thread.
items.cn: spinnan 意为把纤维抽成线。

items.en: The word also described a turning wheel.
items.cn: 这个词也用来形容转动的轮子。

items.en: The spinning of tops and wheels became common.
items.cn: 陀螺与轮子的旋转成为常见用法。

items.en: Spin a story borrowed the thread image.
items.cn: spin a story 借用了纺线的意象。

items.en: Spin-off named a derived product.
items.cn: spin-off 指衍生出来的产品。

note.en: Spin is compared with look-alike words and words for turning.
note.cn: 把 spin 与形近词以及表示转动的词作比较。

entries.definition: the outer covering of a body

normalIntro.en: Spin is one motion: thread, wheel, and story all turn out of it.
normalIntro.cn: spin 是一种动作：线、轮子和故事都从它里面转出来。

normal.en: The top spins on the floor.

abstract.en: A story is thread pulled from the mouth.
abstract.cn: 故事，是从嘴里抽出来的线。

abstract.en: Everything that spins has a still centre.
abstract.cn: 凡旋转之物，都有一个静止的中心。

abstract.en: The wheel forgets it was once wool.
abstract.cn: 轮子忘了自己曾经是羊毛。

examples.en: The wheel spun faster and faster.
examples.cn: 轮子越转越快。

examples.en: She spun wool into thread.
examples.cn: 她把羊毛纺成了线。

examples.en: He spun a tale about a lost city.
examples.cn: 他编了一个关于失落之城的故事。

dict_mnemonic.text: spin 与 spider（蜘蛛）同源，结网就是纺线；spinning top 是陀螺，spin a story 是编故事，spin-off 是衍生作品；注意过去式是 spun。

root: 来自古英语 spinnan（把纤维抽成线），核心义是「抽、转」，后由轮子的转动引申出「旋转」，又由抽线引申出「编造故事」。

sensesIntro.en: Spin means to turn fast, to make thread, or to invent a story.
sensesIntro.cn: spin 指快速旋转、纺线，或编造故事。

core.en: Fibre drawn out and twisted into round motion.
core.cn: 纤维被抽出、拧成环绕的运动。

branches.en: A top hums on the floor.
branches.cn: 陀螺在地面上嗡嗡转。

branches.en: Fingers pull wool into a thin line.
branches.cn: 手指把羊毛拉成细线。

branches.en: A voice draws out an invented tale.
branches.cn: 一个声音把编造的故事拉长。

branches.en: Turning and twisting are the same hand.
branches.cn: 旋转与捻线，是同一只手。

branches.en: Thread and tale are both drawn out.
branches.cn: 线与故事，都是被抽出来的。

intro.en: Spin forms irregular verb parts, agents, and compounds.
intro.cn: spin 构成不规则动词形式、施动名词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Spin has no Latin root; it comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: spin 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语。

items.example: The show led to a spin-off.
items.exampleCN: 这部剧催生了一部衍生剧。

items.meaning: a machine that spins clothes dry
items.example: Put the towels in the spin dryer.
The old spinning wheel still turns.

definition_en: the row of bones down the back, the narrow back edge of a book, or a sharp point on a plant or an animal
core_image: 沿着后背排开的一串尖突骨节
scene: 体检时，医生用手指沿着病人的后背正中往下按，一节一节地数。The doctor ran a finger down the middle of the back and counted each bone of the spine.
sceneCN: 这里 spine 是「脊柱」（第 1 个义项：后背正中那一列椎骨）；句意：体检时，医生用手指沿着后背正中往下按，一节一节数出脊柱的骨头。

derivatives.zh: 脊柱的；由 spine 加形容词词尾 -al 构成，义为与脊柱有关的
无脊椎的；懦弱的；由 spine 加否定词尾 -less 构成
多刺的；由 spine 加形容词词尾 -y 构成，形容长满尖刺

senses.title: The backbone
senses.definition: the row of bones that runs down the back and holds the body upright
senses.definitionCN: 沿后背排列、把身体撑直的一列骨头
senses.example: A fall from the ladder damaged his spine.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，伤了脊柱。
senses.why: Latin spina first named a thorn and then the backbone, because the vertebrae stand out under the skin like a row of small points.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 spina 先指一根刺，再指脊柱，因为一节节椎骨隔着皮肤凸起，就像一排小尖点。

senses.title: The back of a book
senses.definition: the narrow back edge of a book, where the pages are joined together
senses.definitionCN: 书本背面那条窄边，书页在这里被装订在一起
senses.example: The title is printed along the book spine.
senses.exampleCN: 书名印在书脊上。
senses.why: A book spine holds the pages together the way a backbone holds a body, so the same word was borrowed for that narrow edge.
senses.whyCN: 书脊把书页撑在一起，正像脊柱把身体撑起来，于是同一个词被借去指那条窄边。

senses.title: A sharp point
senses.definition: a thin sharp point on a plant or an animal, such as a thorn or a quill
senses.definitionCN: 植物或动物身上细而尖的突起，如荆棘的刺或动物的棘
senses.example: The cactus spines can pierce a thick glove.
senses.exampleCN: 仙人掌的刺能扎穿厚手套。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense of spina, a prickle or thorn, and it is the sharp point from which the whole word family grew.
senses.whyCN: 这是 spina 最古老的含义：一根刺、一个尖点，也是整个词族生长出来的起点。

senses.title: Main support or courage
senses.definition: the central support of a group or thing, or the courage to face a hard situation
senses.definitionCN: 某个团体或事物的核心支撑，也指面对困境时的勇气
senses.example: She showed real spine when she refused the unsafe plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒绝那个不安全的方案时，表现出真正的骨气。
senses.why: If the backbone keeps a body upright, then spine can name whatever keeps a group or a person standing.
senses.whyCN: 既然脊柱让身体挺直，spine 也就能够指让一个团体或一个人挺住的东西。

intro.en: Spine comes from Latin spina, a thorn or prickle that also named the backbone, and reached English through Old French espine.
intro.cn: spine 来自拉丁语 spina（刺、棘，也指脊柱），经古法语 espine 进入英语。

items.en: A reconstructed root, usually written as spei, carried the idea of a sharp point.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根，通常写作 spei，带有「尖点」的意思。

items.en: Spina means a thorn or prickle, and also the backbone of a person or an animal.
items.cn: spina 指刺、棘，也指人或动物的脊柱。

items.en: Anatomists wrote spina dorsi for the spine of the back.
items.cn: 解剖学著作写作 spina dorsi，指背部的脊柱。

items.en: Espine carries the thorn sense into French.
items.cn: espine 把「刺」的含义带进法语。

items.en: Spine appears in English with both the thorn sense and the backbone sense.
items.cn: 中古英语的 spine 同时带有「刺」与「脊柱」两个含义。

items.en: Modern English adds the book spine and the figurative sense of courage or support.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上「书脊」以及「骨气、支柱」的引申义。

note.en: Spine belongs to a Latin family of sharp-point words, and in meaning it stands near backbone, thorn, and vertebra.
note.cn: spine 属于拉丁语中表示「尖点」的词族，在意义上靠近 backbone、thorn 与 vertebra。

entries.definitionCN: 快速旋转；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the row of bones down the back
a sharp point on a plant
one single bone of the spine
entries.definitionCN: 椎骨；脊柱上的一块骨头

normalIntro.en: Spine is the sharp point that turned into a backbone: Latin spina named a thorn first and the back bones second.
normalIntro.cn: spine 是由「尖点」变成的「脊柱」：拉丁语 spina 先指刺，后指背上的骨头。

normal.en: Latin spina means both a thorn and the backbone, because the vertebrae feel like a row of small thorns under the skin.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 spina 既指刺也指脊柱，因为隔着皮肤摸椎骨，就像摸到一排小刺。

normal.en: The book spine is the back of the book, named after the backbone it resembles.
normal.cn: 书脊是书的背面，得名于它像脊柱一样把整体撑住。

normal.en: A spine injury is a damaged backbone, common after a hard fall.
normal.cn: spine injury 是脊柱受伤，重重摔一跤之后很常见。

normal.en: Spinal is the adjective: spinal cord, spinal nerve, spinal column.
normal.cn: spinal 是形容词：spinal cord 脊髓、spinal nerve 脊神经、spinal column 脊柱。

normal.en: Compare thorn: a thorn is a point on a plant, while spine covers plants, animals, the backbone, and a book.
normal.cn: 对比 thorn：thorn 专指植物的刺，spine 则覆盖植物、动物、脊柱与书脊。

abstract.en: Picture your hand running down the middle of a back and finding a row of small knobs.
abstract.cn: 想象手掌沿着后背正中往下滑，摸到一排凸起的小骨节。

abstract.en: Picture a closed book standing upright, its narrow back facing you like a straight spine.
abstract.cn: 想象一本合上的书立起来，窄窄的书脊朝向你，像一根笔直的脊柱。

abstract.en: Picture a cactus pad with one thin needle just touching a fingertip.
abstract.cn: 想象仙人掌的一片掌上，一根细针正碰到指尖。

examples.en: He injured his spine in a fall from the ladder.
examples.cn: 他从梯子上摔下来，伤了脊柱。

examples.en: The book spine was cracked and the pages came loose.
examples.cn: 那本书的书脊裂了，书页松脱下来。

examples.en: Cactus spines keep animals from eating the plant.
examples.cn: 仙人掌的刺让动物没法啃食这株植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「死拼」——拼到脊柱都伤了；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语 spina 无关。

root: 拉丁语 spina（刺、棘，也指脊柱）→ 古法语 espine（刺）→ 中古英语 spine → 现代英语 spine；核心义是「尖起的骨节」，由刺扩展到脊柱、书脊与骨气。

sensesIntro.en: Spine starts from the sharp point named by Latin spina, then covers the backbone, the back of a book, and finally the idea of support or courage.
sensesIntro.cn: spine 从拉丁语 spina 的「尖刺」出发，先指脊柱，再指书脊，最后引申为支撑与骨气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of small sharp knobs standing along the back.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿着后背排开的一串小小尖突。

branches.en: The backbone is the anatomical core of the word.
branches.cn: 脊柱是这个词在解剖学上的核心义。

branches.en: The book spine borrows the shape of a backbone.
branches.cn: 书脊义借用了脊柱的形状。

branches.en: The sharp point is the oldest sense of the Latin source.
branches.cn: 尖刺义是拉丁语来源中最古老的义项。

branches.en: A backbone is literally a row of pointed bones, so the two senses share one shape.
branches.cn: 脊柱本来就是一串带尖的骨头，所以这两个义项共用同一个形状。

branches.en: A book spine and a personal spine both hold something upright.
branches.cn: 书脊与人的骨气都在把东西撑直。

intro.en: Spine is a Latin sharp-point noun, and English builds spinal, spinous, spiny, and spineless around it.
intro.cn: spine 是拉丁语中表示「尖点」的名词，英语围绕它构成 spinal、spinous、spiny 与 spineless。

latinIntro.en: Latin spina means a thorn or prickle, and by extension the backbone that looks like a row of them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spina 意为刺、棘，并引申指像一排刺的脊柱。

items.example: Spina is the Latin source of spine.
items.exampleCN: spina 是 spine 的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Anatomists still use spina dorsi for the backbone.
items.exampleCN: 解剖学至今仍用 spina dorsi 指背脊。

items.example: Old French espine carried the thorn sense.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 espine 保留了「刺」的含义。

items.example: Spine gathers all three senses in English.
items.exampleCN: spine 在英语里汇集了这三个义项。

items.example: Spinal means belonging to the backbone.
items.exampleCN: spinal 意为与脊柱有关的。

items.example: The suffix -al turns spine into spinal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 spine 变成 spinal。

items.meaning: full of spines or sharp points

items.example: A spiny cactus guards its water.
items.exampleCN: 多刺的仙人掌守护着自己的水分。

definition_en: relating to the spirit, the inner self, or religion
core_image: 烛光在安静的教堂里缓缓升起
scene: 音乐对她的心灵有很深的影响。Music has a deep spiritual effect on her.
sceneCN: 这里 spiritual 是「精神的、心灵的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：音乐对她的心灵有很深的影响。

pos.zh: 灵性的；有深层感染力的

senses.title: Of the inner self
senses.definition: relating to the inner self rather than the body
senses.definitionCN: 关乎内在自我而非肉体的
senses.example: Music has a deep spiritual effect on her.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐对她的心灵有很深的影响。
senses.why: The core sense points inward, beyond the body.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的用法，指向肉体之外的内在。

senses.title: Of religion
senses.definition: relating to religion or religious practice
senses.definitionCN: 与宗教或宗教活动有关的
senses.example: He studied spiritual writings from the East.
senses.exampleCN: 他研读来自东方的宗教著作。
senses.why: Institutions of faith give the word a public sense.
senses.whyCN: 信仰的制度化让这个词带上公共宗教义。

senses.title: Deeply moving
senses.definition: showing a calm, deeply felt quality
senses.definitionCN: 带有宁静而深切感染力的
senses.example: There was a spiritual calm in the old garden.
senses.exampleCN: 老花园里有一种心灵的宁静。
senses.why: The inner sense extends to places and atmospheres.
senses.whyCN: 内在之义扩展到场所与氛围。

intro.en: Spiritual comes from Latin spiritualis, of breath or spirit.
intro.cn: spiritual 来自拉丁语 spiritualis，意为气息或精神的。

items.en: Spiritus meant breath and the breath of life.
items.cn: spiritus 意为气息与生命之气。

items.en: Spiritualis described what belongs to the spirit.
items.cn: spiritualis 形容属于精神的事物。

items.en: Spirituel carried the word into French.
items.cn: spirituel 把这个词带进法语。

items.en: Spiritual entered English in religious use.
items.cn: spiritual 以宗教用法进入英语。

items.en: It broadened to inner peace and depth of feeling.
items.cn: 后来扩展到内心的平静与情感深度。

note.en: Spiritual is compared with look-alike words and words for the sacred.
note.cn: 把 spiritual 与形近词以及表示神圣的词语作比较。

normalIntro.en: Spiritual is spirit wearing an adjective.
normalIntro.cn: spiritual 就是穿上形容词外衣的 spirit。

normal.cn: 他们唱了一首宗教歌曲。

normal.en: The place has a spiritual feel.
normal.cn: 这个地方有灵性的气息。

abstract.en: The body is seen; the spiritual is felt.
abstract.cn: 身体看得见，精神只能感到。

abstract.en: A quiet room can be a church.
abstract.cn: 一间安静的房间，也可以是一座教堂。

abstract.en: What feeds the spirit leaves no crumbs.
abstract.cn: 喂养精神的东西，不留碎屑。

examples.en: Music has a deep spiritual effect on her.
examples.cn: 音乐对她的心灵有很深的影响。

examples.en: He studied spiritual writings from the East.
examples.cn: 他研读来自东方的宗教著作。

examples.en: There was a spiritual calm in the old garden.
examples.cn: 老花园里有一种心灵的宁静。

dict_mnemonic.text: spiritual 由 spirit（精神）加 -ual 构成，同族词有 spiritually（精神上）、spirituality（灵性）；spiritual life 是精神生活，spiritual leader 是精神领袖。

root: 来自拉丁语 spiritualis（属于精神的），词根 spiritus 意为气息；核心义为「关乎内在之气的」，后分为宗教义与心灵深度义。

sensesIntro.en: Spiritual means of the inner self, of religion, or deeply moving in a quiet way.
sensesIntro.cn: spiritual 指关乎内在自我、关乎宗教，或带有宁静的感染力。

core.en: Belonging to the breath inside a person.
core.cn: 属于人体内那口气的。

branches.en: Music moves something deeper than the ear.
branches.cn: 音乐触动了比耳朵更深的地方。

branches.en: A choir sings under a high ceiling.
branches.cn: 唱诗班在高高的穹顶下歌唱。

branches.en: An old garden holds a hush.
branches.cn: 老花园里藏着一片寂静。

branches.en: The inner life and the shared faith meet.
branches.cn: 内在生活与共同信仰在此相遇。

branches.en: Belief and calm can share one room.
branches.cn: 信仰与宁静，可以同处一室。

intro.en: Spiritual forms adverbs, nouns, and further derivatives.
intro.cn: spiritual 构成副词、名词和进一步的派生词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is spiritus, breath.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 spiritus，意为气息。

items.exampleCN: 他们在精神上共同成长。
唯灵论在那个世纪传播开来。
一位唯灵论者主持了聚会。
诗歌能让日常生活精神化。

definition_en: to force saliva out of the mouth, or a rod for roasting meat

scene: 他吐掉了苦涩的药片。He spat out the bitter pill.

senses.title: Send out saliva

senses.why: The basic bodily action is the core sense.

senses.title: Spit something out

senses.definitionCN: 把嘴里的东西吐出来
senses.example: He spat out the bitter pill.
senses.exampleCN: 他吐掉了苦涩的药片。
senses.why: The action takes an object, often something unwanted.
senses.whyCN: 带宾语时指吐出不要的东西。

senses.title: A roasting rod
senses.definition: a thin rod used to hold meat over a fire
senses.definitionCN: 用来把肉架在火上烤的细杆
senses.example: The meat turned slowly on the spit.

senses.why: The noun names an old cooking tool.
senses.whyCN: 名词义指一种古老的炊具。

items.en: Spittan meant to spit.
items.cn: spittan 意为吐唾沫。

items.en: The verb kept the same bodily sense.

items.en: Spit out extended it to any object in the mouth.

items.en: Spit and polish described hard cleaning.
items.cn: spit and polish 形容费力擦洗。

items.en: The noun spit kept the roasting rod sense.
items.cn: 名词 spit 保留了烤肉叉之义。

note.en: Spit is compared with look-alike words and words for the mouth.
note.cn: 把 spit 与形近词以及表示口腔动作的词作比较。

entries.definition: to send out in a rush
to push air out of the throat
to let saliva run from the mouth

normalIntro.en: Spit is the mouth throwing something out.
normalIntro.cn: spit 就是嘴巴把东西扔出去。

normal.en: The meat turned on the spit.
The cat spat at the dog.

abstract.en: Some words are spat, not spoken.
abstract.cn: 有些话是吐出来的，不是说出来的。

abstract.en: A bitter taste is refused by the tongue.
abstract.cn: 苦味会被舌头拒绝。

abstract.en: Fire and spit both turn meat into food.

examples.en: He spat on the ground.
examples.cn: 他往地上吐了口唾沫。

examples.en: He spat out the bitter pill.
examples.cn: 他吐掉了苦涩的药片。

examples.en: The meat turned slowly on the spit.
examples.cn: 肉在烤肉叉上慢慢转动。

root: 来自古英语 spittan（吐唾沫），核心义是口腔把东西送出去，名词义「烤肉叉」来自另一条同形词源。

sensesIntro.en: Spit means to send out saliva, to spit something out, or a rod for roasting.
sensesIntro.cn: spit 指吐唾沫、吐出东西，或烤肉叉。

core.en: The mouth pushing matter away.
core.cn: 嘴巴把东西推开。

branches.en: A drop of saliva hits the dust.
branches.cn: 一滴唾液落进尘土。

branches.en: A bitter pill leaves the tongue.
branches.cn: 苦药片离开了舌头。

branches.en: Meat turns above red coals.
branches.cn: 肉在红炭上方转动。

branches.en: Saliva and objects leave by one motion.
branches.cn: 唾液与物件，以同一种动作离开。

branches.en: One spit rejects, the other feeds.
branches.cn: 一个 spit 在拒绝，另一个在供养。

intro.en: Spit forms irregular verb parts and compound nouns.
intro.cn: spit 构成不规则动词形式和复合名词。

latinIntro.en: Spit has no Latin root; it comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: spit 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语。

items.example: The cat is spitting at us.

items.exampleCN: 唾液顺着他的下巴流下。

items.example: He threw a spitball in class.
items.exampleCN: 他在课上扔了个纸团弹。

items.example: An old spittoon stood in the corner.
items.exampleCN: 角落里放着一个旧痰盂。

definition_zh: 恶意；怨恨；不顾（in spite of）
definition_en: a wish to hurt or annoy someone; in spite of means despite
core_image: 一双冷冷盯着人的眼睛
scene: 尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。They set off in spite of the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 spite 是「不顾、尽管」（第 3 个义项）；句意：尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。

senses.title: Wish to hurt
senses.definition: a desire to hurt or annoy another person
senses.definitionCN: 想伤害或惹恼别人的心思
senses.example: He broke the vase out of spite.
senses.exampleCN: 他出于恶意打碎了花瓶。
senses.why: The core sense is small, active ill will.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项，指主动的小恶意。

senses.title: Lasting resentment
senses.definition: a lasting feeling of resentment
senses.definitionCN: 持续不散的怨恨情绪
senses.example: There was spite in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的声音里带着怨气。
senses.why: The feeling is seen as stored rather than acted out.
senses.whyCN: 这种情绪被看作积存的，而非当下发作。

senses.title: Despite
senses.definition: used in the phrase in spite of, meaning despite
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 in spite of，意为尽管、不顾
senses.example: They set off in spite of the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。
senses.why: The phrase turns ill will into resistance to a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把恶意转化为对事实的抗拒。

intro.en: Spite comes from Old French despit, meaning contempt.
intro.cn: spite 来自古法语 despit，意为轻蔑。

items.en: Despectus meant a looking down on others.
items.cn: despectus 意为俯视、轻视。

items.en: Despit named contempt and ill will.
items.cn: despit 指轻蔑与恶意。

items.en: Spite entered English as a word for malice.
items.cn: spite 以「恶意」之义进入英语。

items.en: In spite of came to mean despite.
items.cn: in spite of 逐渐表示「尽管」。

items.en: Spiteful described a person full of ill will.
items.cn: spiteful 形容满怀恶意的人。

note.en: Spite is compared with look-alike words and words for ill will.
note.cn: 把 spite 与形近词以及表示恶意的词作比较。

entries.definition: to send saliva from the mouth

normalIntro.en: Spite is anger kept for later.
normalIntro.cn: spite 是留到以后用的怒气。

normal.en: He did it out of spite.
We went out in spite of the rain.
normal.cn: 尽管下雨我们还是出去了。

normal.en: Spite made him refuse the offer.
normal.cn: 赌气让他拒绝了那个提议。

abstract.en: Spite drinks its own poison first.
abstract.cn: 怨恨先喝下自己的毒药。

abstract.en: In spite of the rain, the road still leads on.
abstract.cn: 尽管下雨，路仍向前。

abstract.en: Small malice leaves the longest marks.
abstract.cn: 小小的恶意，留下最长的痕迹。

examples.en: He broke the vase out of spite.
examples.cn: 他出于恶意打碎了花瓶。

examples.en: There was spite in her voice.
examples.cn: 她的声音里带着怨气。

examples.en: They set off in spite of the rain.
examples.cn: 尽管下雨，他们还是出发了。

dict_mnemonic.text: spite 是「恶意」，out of spite 是「出于恶意」；in spite of 是固定短语，意为「尽管」，相当于 despite；spiteful 是形容词「恶意的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 despectus（轻视），经古法语 despit 进入英语，核心义为「轻蔑带来的恶意」，短语 in spite of 又发展出「尽管」。

sensesIntro.en: Spite means petty ill will, stored resentment, or, in in spite of, despite.
sensesIntro.cn: spite 指小恶意、积存的怨恨，或在 in spite of 中表示尽管。

core.en: Contempt turned into a small weapon.
core.cn: 轻蔑变成的一件小武器。

branches.en: A hand breaks what it cannot have.
branches.cn: 得不到的手，干脆把它打碎。

branches.en: An old insult is kept warm.
branches.cn: 旧日的冒犯被一直焐着。

branches.en: Rain falls, yet the walk goes on.
branches.cn: 雨在下，脚步却没有停。

branches.en: Malice and memory feed each other.
branches.cn: 恶意与记忆，互相喂养。

branches.en: Resentment hardens into refusal.
branches.cn: 怨恨硬化成了抗拒。

intro.en: Spite forms adjectives, adverbs, and nouns.
intro.cn: spite 构成形容词、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is despectus, a looking down.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 despectus，意为俯视、轻视。

items.example: He did it out of spite.

items.exampleCN: 小小的恶意让老朋友疏远。

items.example: He felt spited by the remark.
items.exampleCN: 他觉得自己被那句话恶意中伤。
尽管下雨，他们还是走了。

definition_en: very impressive and beautiful, or excellent
core_image: 夕阳把整片山谷染成金色
scene: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。The sunset made the valley splendid.
sceneCN: 这里 splendid 是「壮丽的、辉煌的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。

senses.title: Magnificent to see
senses.definition: magnificent and impressive to look at
senses.definitionCN: 看上去宏伟而令人赞叹的
senses.example: The sunset made the valley splendid.
senses.exampleCN: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。
senses.why: The core sense comes from shining beauty.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项源于光彩夺目的美。

senses.title: Very good
senses.definition: excellent, used especially in spoken praise
senses.definitionCN: 极好的，多用于口头称赞
senses.example: That is a splendid idea.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个绝妙的主意。
senses.why: The visual sense weakens into general praise.
senses.whyCN: 视觉义弱化，变成一般性的称赞。

senses.title: Rich in style
senses.definition: rich and impressive in style or decoration
senses.definitionCN: 风格或装饰富丽堂皇的
senses.example: The hall had a splendid ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅有一个华丽的天花板。
senses.why: The sense stays visual but moves to built things.
senses.whyCN: 仍属视觉义，但转向人造之物。

intro.en: Splendid comes from Latin splendidus, meaning shining.
intro.cn: splendid 来自拉丁语 splendidus，意为闪光的。

items.en: Splendere meant to shine or glow.
items.cn: splendere 意为发光、闪耀。

items.en: Splendidus described something bright and fine.
items.cn: splendidus 形容明亮而精美之物。

items.en: Splendid entered English as shining and fine.
items.cn: splendid 以「明亮精美」之义进入英语。

items.en: It broadened to mean magnificent.
items.cn: 词义扩展为「宏伟壮丽」。

items.en: It also became a polite word of praise.
items.cn: 它又成为礼貌的称赞用语。

note.en: Splendid is compared with look-alike words and words for beauty.
note.cn: 把 splendid 与形近词以及表示华美的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Splendid is light made into a compliment.
normalIntro.cn: splendid 是被说成赞美的光。

normal.en: They live in a splendid house.
normal.cn: 他们住在一座华丽的房子里。

normal.en: The garden looks splendid in spring.
normal.cn: 春天的花园看起来美极了。

abstract.en: Splendour is a light that stays after sunset.
abstract.cn: 辉煌，是日落之后仍留着的光。

abstract.en: Praise borrows the words of sunlight.
abstract.cn: 赞美借用了阳光的词汇。

abstract.en: The finest halls are quiet inside.
abstract.cn: 最华丽的厅堂，内里最安静。

examples.en: The sunset made the valley splendid.
examples.cn: 夕阳把山谷照得一片辉煌。

examples.en: That is a splendid idea.
examples.cn: 那是个绝妙的主意。

examples.en: The hall had a splendid ceiling.
examples.cn: 大厅有一个华丽的天花板。

dict_mnemonic.text: splendid 与 splendour（壮丽）同根，词根意为「发光」；splendid view 是壮丽景色，splendid idea 是绝妙主意；口语中常用作「极好的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 splendidus（闪光的），词根 splendere 意为发光，核心义由「光彩夺目」扩展到「壮丽」与「极好」。

sensesIntro.en: Splendid means magnificent to see, excellent, or rich in style.
sensesIntro.cn: splendid 指外观壮丽、极好，或风格华丽。

core.en: Light that makes people stop and look.
core.cn: 让人停下来看的光。

branches.en: Gold spreads over the valley.
branches.cn: 金色铺满山谷。

branches.en: A voice says, what a good idea.
branches.cn: 一个声音说，这主意真好。

branches.en: Carved ceilings catch the candlelight.
branches.cn: 雕花天花板接住烛光。

branches.en: Nature and craft both aim at glory.
branches.cn: 自然与工艺，都朝着辉煌。

branches.en: Praise and ornament share one brightness.
branches.cn: 赞美与装饰，共用一种明亮。

intro.en: Splendid forms comparison, nouns, and adverbs.
intro.cn: splendid 构成比较级、名词和副词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is splendere, to shine.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 splendere，意为发光。

items.example: The view grew splendider at dusk.
The splendidness of the scene struck us.
items.exampleCN: 景色的壮丽震撼了我们。

items.example: A splendorous dawn lit the sea.
items.exampleCN: 辉煌的黎明照亮了海面。

definition_en: to divide or break into parts
core_image: 斧头落下，木柴裂成两半
scene: 他把木头劈成两半。He split the wood in two.
sceneCN: 这里 split 是「劈开」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把木头劈成两半。

senses.title: Break apart
senses.definition: to divide or break something along a line
senses.definitionCN: 沿一条线把某物分开或劈断
senses.example: He split the wood in two.
senses.exampleCN: 他把木头劈成两半。
senses.why: The core sense is a physical break.
senses.whyCN: 最核心的义项是物理上的断开。

senses.title: Divide into groups
senses.definition: to divide into separate groups or parts
senses.definitionCN: 分裂成不同的群体或部分
senses.example: The party split over the issue.
senses.exampleCN: 该党在这个问题上分裂了。
senses.why: The physical break is applied to people and groups.
senses.whyCN: 把物理的断裂用在人与群体上。

senses.title: Share the cost
senses.definition: to share something among several people
senses.definitionCN: 在几个人之间分配某物
senses.example: We split the bill between us.
senses.exampleCN: 我们平摊了账单。
senses.why: Dividing a sum is the everyday financial sense.
senses.whyCN: 把钱分开，是最日常的经济义。

intro.en: Split comes from a Low German verb meaning to cleave.
intro.cn: split 来自低地德语动词，意为劈开。

items.en: Splitten meant to split or cleave.
items.cn: splitten 意为劈开、裂开。

items.en: Splijten carried the same sense.
items.cn: splijten 有相同的含义。

items.en: The verb entered English as splitten.
items.cn: 这个词以 splitten 进入英语。

items.en: It extended from wood to groups and money.
items.cn: 词义从木头扩展到群体与金钱。

items.en: Split second named a tiny division of time.
items.cn: split second 指极短的一瞬。

note.en: Split is compared with look-alike words and words for dividing.
note.cn: 把 split 与形近词以及表示分开的词作比较。

entries.definition: to send saliva from the mouth

normalIntro.en: Split is one thing becoming two.
normalIntro.cn: split 就是一个东西变成两个。

normal.en: Split the log with an axe.
He ran in a split second.

abstract.en: Every split leaves two edges.
abstract.cn: 每一次裂开，都留下两道边。

abstract.en: Two halves remember being one.
abstract.cn: 两半都记得曾是一体。

abstract.en: A bill divided is easier to carry.
abstract.cn: 分开的账单，更好扛。

examples.en: He split the wood in two.
examples.cn: 他把木头劈成两半。

examples.en: The party split over the issue.
examples.cn: 该党在这个问题上分裂了。

examples.en: We split the bill between us.
examples.cn: 我们平摊了账单。

dict_mnemonic.text: split 的过去式和过去分词都是 split；split up 是「分手、分开」，split the bill 是「平摊账单」，split hairs 是「吹毛求疵」，split second 是「一瞬间」。

root: 来自低地德语 splitten（劈开），与荷兰语 splijten 同源，核心义为「一分为二」，后扩展为群体分裂与费用分摊。

sensesIntro.en: Split means to break apart, to divide into groups, or to share a cost.
sensesIntro.cn: split 指劈开、分裂成群体，或分摊费用。

core.en: One body cut into two.
core.cn: 一个整体被切成两半。

branches.en: The axe meets the log.
branches.cn: 斧头劈中木头。

branches.en: One group walks out of another.
branches.cn: 一群人从另一群人中走出。

branches.en: Two friends count coins at a table.
branches.cn: 两个朋友在桌边数硬币。

branches.en: Wood and parties break along a seam.
branches.cn: 木头与党派，都沿一道缝裂开。

branches.en: What is divided must be shared.
branches.cn: 被分开的，总要被分担。

intro.en: Split forms third-person, participle, and compound words.
intro.cn: split 构成第三人称、分词和复合词。

latinIntro.en: Split has no Latin root; it comes from Low German.
latinIntro.cn: split 没有拉丁词根，它来自低地德语。

items.example: Split the log with an axe.

items.exampleCN: 他们的分手让所有人吃惊。
他们买了一栋错层房子。

items.meaning: a dried pea split in half

items.example: The film shows a split personality.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影表现了一个分裂的人格。

definition_en: to harm someone's character with too much kindness, or to ruin something
core_image: 被惯坏的孩子把玩具扔了一地
scene: 祖父母把孙子宠坏了。The grandparents spoil their grandson.
sceneCN: 这里 spoil 是「宠坏、溺爱」（第 1 个义项）；句意：祖父母把孙子宠坏了。

senses.title: Ruin with kindness
senses.definition: to harm someone's character by giving too much
senses.definitionCN: 因给予过多而损害某人的性格
senses.example: The grandparents spoil their grandson.
senses.exampleCN: 祖父母把孙子宠坏了。
senses.why: This sense is central in family talk.
senses.whyCN: 这是家庭语境中最核心的用法。

senses.title: Ruin an event
senses.definition: to damage or ruin something
senses.definitionCN: 损坏或毁掉某事
senses.example: The rain spoiled our picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 这场雨毁了我们的野餐。
senses.why: The older sense is direct damage.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的义项是直接的损坏。

senses.title: Go bad
senses.definition: to become bad or unfit to eat
senses.definitionCN: 变坏、不再适合食用
senses.example: The fruit will spoil in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 水果在高温下会变质。
senses.why: Food damage happens without anyone acting.
senses.whyCN: 食物变坏是无人动手也会发生的事。

intro.en: Spoil comes from Latin spoliare, to strip or plunder.
intro.cn: spoil 来自拉丁语 spoliare，意为剥夺、掠夺。

items.en: Spoliare meant to strip or rob.
items.cn: spoliare 意为剥夺、抢劫。

items.en: Espoillier meant to plunder.
items.cn: espoillier 意为掠夺。

items.en: Spoilen meant to rob or damage.
items.cn: spoil 在中古英语中意为抢劫、损坏。

items.en: The sense softened to harming character.
items.cn: 词义柔化为损害性格。

items.en: Food spoiling meant going bad.
items.cn: 食物 spoil 表示变质。

note.en: Spoil is compared with look-alike words and words for ruining.
note.cn: 把 spoil 与形近词以及表示毁坏的词作比较。

entries.definition: to treat with too much care

normalIntro.en: Spoil once meant to plunder; now it means to damage with too much.
normalIntro.cn: spoil 原意是掠夺，如今指用过多的给予把人毁掉。

normal.en: He spoiled the ending for me.

normal.cn: 我们选择多得不知挑哪个。

abstract.en: Too much sweetness spoils the dish.
abstract.cn: 太甜，会毁了一道菜。

abstract.en: What is never refused is never valued.
abstract.cn: 从不被拒绝的，也不会被珍惜。

abstract.en: Fruit and favor both turn with time.
abstract.cn: 水果与恩宠，都会随时间变味。

examples.en: The grandparents spoil their grandson.
examples.cn: 祖父母把孙子宠坏了。

examples.en: The rain spoiled our picnic.
examples.cn: 这场雨毁了我们的野餐。

examples.en: The fruit will spoil in the heat.
examples.cn: 水果在高温下会变质。

root: 来自拉丁语 spoliare（剥夺、掠夺），经古法语 espoillier 进入英语，核心义由「抢劫、损坏」软化为「宠坏、破坏、变质」。

sensesIntro.en: Spoil means to ruin a person with kindness, to damage an event, or to go bad.
sensesIntro.cn: spoil 指用溺爱毁掉一个人、破坏某事，或食物变质。

core.en: Damage done by taking or giving too much.
core.cn: 取之过多或给之过多造成的损坏。

branches.en: A child throws a toy and laughs.
branches.cn: 孩子扔了玩具还在笑。

branches.en: Rain falls on a laid table.
branches.cn: 雨落在摆好的餐桌上。

branches.en: Fruit softens in a warm bowl.
branches.cn: 水果在温热的碗里变软。

branches.en: Too much care and too much rain both ruin.
branches.cn: 过多的照顾与过多的雨，都会毁掉。

branches.en: What is damaged may also decay.
branches.cn: 被损坏的，也会继续腐坏。

intro.en: Spoil forms verb parts, adjectives, and nouns.
intro.cn: spoil 构成动词变化、形容词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is spoliare, to strip.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 spoliare，意为剥夺。

items.example: Too much praise spoils a person.
items.exampleCN: 过多的赞美会毁掉一个人。

items.meaning: one who spoils, or a plot leak

definition_en: a person or company that pays for an event or supports someone
core_image: 一块印着品牌名的赛事背景板
scene: 这家银行是比赛的赞助商。The bank is a sponsor of the race.
sceneCN: 这里 sponsor 是「赞助商」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家银行是比赛的赞助商。

senses.title: A financial backer
senses.definition: a person or company that pays for an event
senses.definitionCN: 为活动出资的个人或公司
senses.example: The bank is a sponsor of the race.

examples.en: The prize was a spur to work harder.
examples.cn: 这份奖品是更努力工作的刺激。

examples.en: The rider touched the horse with his spurs.
examples.cn: 骑手用马刺轻碰马身。

examples.en: Curiosity spurred her to keep learning.
examples.cn: 好奇心促使她继续学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: spur 是「马刺」，引申为「刺激、激励」；spur on 是激励，spur growth 是促进增长，spur of the moment 是一时冲动；过去式是 spurred。

root: 来自古英语 spura（马刺），与古诺尔斯语 spori 同源，核心义为靴跟上的尖刺，后引申为任何促人行动的刺激。

sensesIntro.en: Spur means a stimulus, a rider's spiked tool, or to urge someone forward.
sensesIntro.cn: spur 指刺激、马刺，或激励某人向前。

core.en: A small point that starts a large motion.
core.cn: 启动巨大运动的一个小尖点。

branches.en: A prize waits on a shelf.
branches.cn: 奖品摆在架子上。

branches.en: Metal shines at a rider's heel.
branches.cn: 金属在骑手靴跟闪光。

branches.en: A question sends a student back to books.
branches.cn: 一个问题把学生送回书本。

branches.en: The tool and the motive are one image.
branches.cn: 工具与动机，是同一个意象。

branches.en: A touch becomes a command to move.
branches.cn: 轻轻一碰，变成前进的命令。

intro.en: Spur forms verb parts and a few compounds.
intro.cn: spur 构成动词变化和少量复合词。

latinIntro.en: Spur has no Latin root; it is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: spur 没有拉丁词根，它属日耳曼语。

items.example: The coach kept spurring the team.

items.exampleCN: 年轻的骑手没有戴马刺。

items.example: The machine uses a spur gear.
A spur track leads to the mill.

definition_zh: 正方形；广场；平方；公正的
definition_en: a shape with four equal sides, an open city space, or fair and honest
core_image: 广场地砖拼成整齐的正方形
scene: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。The children flew kites in the square.
sceneCN: 这里 square 是「广场」（第 2 个义项）；句意：孩子们在广场上放风筝。

senses.title: Four-sided shape
senses.definition: a shape with four equal sides and four right angles
senses.definitionCN: 四条边相等、四个角都是直角的图形
senses.example: She drew a square on the board.
senses.exampleCN: 她在黑板上画了一个正方形。
senses.why: This is the concrete shape sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的形状义项。

senses.title: Open city space
senses.definition: an open area in a town, often with buildings around it
senses.definitionCN: 城镇中四周常有建筑的开阔场地
senses.example: The children flew kites in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。
senses.why: The shape became a place in old towns.
senses.whyCN: 在古老城镇里，方形的地块变成了场所。

senses.title: Product of a number
senses.definition: the result of multiplying a number by itself
senses.definitionCN: 一个数自乘所得的结果
senses.example: Five squared is twenty-five.
senses.exampleCN: 五的平方是二十五。
senses.why: A square number is drawn as a square array.
senses.whyCN: 平方数可以排成正方形点阵。

senses.title: Fair and honest
senses.definition: honest and fair in dealing with people
senses.definitionCN: 待人处事诚实公平的
senses.example: It was a square deal for both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双方都是公平的交易。
senses.why: A right angle suggests straight and fair conduct.
senses.whyCN: 直角象征正直、公平的行为。

intro.en: Square comes from Latin exquadrare, to make square, through Old French esquarre.
intro.cn: square 经古法语 esquarre 来自拉丁语 exquadrare，意为使成方形。

items.en: Exquadrare meant to make square.
items.cn: exquadrare 意为使成方形。

items.en: Esquarre meant a square or a rule.
items.cn: esquarre 意为方形或曲尺。

items.en: Square named the shape and the tool.
items.cn: square 既指形状也指工具。

items.en: The open place sense grew in towns.
items.cn: 「广场」义项在城镇中发展起来。

items.en: The fair sense came from honest measure.
items.cn: 「公正」义项来自诚实的度量。

note.en: Square is compared with look-alike words and words for open places.
note.cn: 把 square 与形近词以及表示开阔场地的词作比较。

entries.definition: a shape with four right angles

normalIntro.en: Square is a right-angled shape, a town space, a number, and a fair deal.
normalIntro.cn: square 是直角图形、城镇空地、平方数，也是公平的交易。

normal.en: Fold the paper into a square.
We met in the town square.
The room is twelve square metres.
normal.cn: 这个房间有十二平方米。

abstract.en: Equal sides make a steady shape.
abstract.cn: 相等的边构成稳固的图形。

abstract.en: A square deal needs two honest sides.
abstract.cn: 公平的交易需要双方都诚实。

abstract.en: Every number can grow into a square.
abstract.cn: 每个数都能长成自己的平方。

examples.en: She drew a square on the board.
examples.cn: 她在黑板上画了一个正方形。

examples.en: The children flew kites in the square.
examples.cn: 孩子们在广场上放风筝。

examples.en: It was a square deal for both sides.
examples.cn: 这对双方都是公平的交易。

dict_mnemonic.text: square 基本义是「正方形」，由此引申出广场、平方和公正；town square 是城镇广场，square root 是平方根，fair and square 是光明正大。

root: 经古法语 esquarre 来自拉丁语 exquadrare（使成方形），词根 quadr- 表示四；由「四边相等的图形」引申出广场、平方和公正。

sensesIntro.en: Square names a shape, a town space, a product of multiplication, or fair conduct.
sensesIntro.cn: square 指正方形、广场、平方数，或公正的行为。

core.en: Four equal sides meeting at right angles.
core.cn: 四条相等的边以直角相接。

branches.en: A child draws four even lines.
branches.cn: 孩子画出四条等长的线。

branches.en: Paving stones mark a wide open place.
branches.cn: 铺路石围出一片开阔场地。

branches.en: Dots form an even block of rows.
branches.cn: 圆点排成整齐的方阵。

branches.en: A level table suggests an honest deal.
branches.cn: 平稳的桌面象征公平的交易。

branches.en: The shape and the number share one form.
branches.cn: 图形与数字共享同一种形态。

intro.en: Square forms plurals, comparisons, adverbs, and a noun.
intro.cn: square 构成复数、比较级、副词和名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is exquadrare, to make square.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 exquadrare，意为使成方形。

items.example: The board is full of squares.

items.exampleCN: 求一个数的平方很容易。

items.example: This table is squarer than that one.
items.exampleCN: 这张桌子比那张更方正。

items.example: It is the squarest room in the house.
items.exampleCN: 这是屋里最方正的房间。

items.example: The squareness of the box pleased her.

latinEntries.exampleCN: 他们想把石头凿成方形。

definition_en: to press something firmly, to get liquid out, or to force your way into a small space
core_image: 双手把柠檬挤出一滴汁
scene: 她挤了一点柠檬汁。She squeezed a little lemon juice.
sceneCN: 这里 squeeze 是「挤压、榨取」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她挤了一点柠檬汁。

senses.title: Press firmly
senses.definition: to press something hard from both sides
senses.definitionCN: 从两边用力压某物
senses.example: She squeezed the lemon gently.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻轻挤压柠檬。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Force out
senses.definition: to get liquid or money out by pressure
senses.definitionCN: 靠压力取得液体或钱财
senses.example: They squeezed more money from the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从预算里又榨出一些钱。
senses.why: Pressure applied to people yields money too.
senses.whyCN: 对人施压也能得到钱财。

senses.title: Crowd in
senses.definition: to force yourself into a narrow space
senses.definitionCN: 勉强进入狭窄空间
senses.example: We squeezed into the last seats.
senses.exampleCN: 我们挤进了最后几个座位。
senses.why: A body under pressure fits a small space.
senses.whyCN: 身体受压就能塞进狭小空间。

intro.en: Squeeze comes from Old English cwysan, to press, of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: squeeze 来自古英语 cwysan（压），更深来源不确定。

items.en: The deeper origin of the word is unknown.
items.cn: 这个词的更早来源已不可考。

items.en: Cwysan meant to press or crush.
items.cn: cwysan 意为压或压碎。

items.en: The form became queisen or squeezen.
items.cn: 词形演变为 queisen 或 squeezen。

items.en: Squeeze kept the sense of pressing hard.
items.cn: squeeze 保留了用力压的含义。

items.en: The money sense grew from pressure on people.
items.cn: 「榨取钱财」义由向人施压引申而来。

note.en: Squeeze is compared with look-alike words and words for pressing.
note.cn: 把 squeeze 与形近词以及表示压挤的词作比较。

entries.definition: a shape with four equal sides
to blow air out of the nose

normalIntro.en: Squeeze is pressure from two sides, whether on fruit, money, or space.
normalIntro.cn: squeeze 是两侧的压力，无论压在水果、钱财还是空间上。

normal.en: Squeeze the lemon into the tea.

normal.cn: 他紧紧握了一下我的手。

normal.en: We squeezed into a tiny car.

abstract.en: Pressure brings out what is inside.
abstract.cn: 压力能逼出里面的东西。

abstract.en: A narrow door still lets people through.
abstract.cn: 窄门仍能让人通过。

abstract.en: Too much squeezing leaves a dry fruit.
abstract.cn: 挤得太狠，果子就干了。

examples.en: She squeezed the lemon gently.
examples.cn: 她轻轻挤压柠檬。

examples.en: They squeezed more money from the budget.
examples.cn: 他们从预算里又榨出一些钱。

examples.en: We squeezed into the last seats.
examples.cn: 我们挤进了最后几个座位。

dict_mnemonic.text: squeeze 是「挤压、榨取、挤进」；squeeze out 是挤出，squeeze into 是挤进，a tight squeeze 是拥挤难行；过去式加 d 变 squeezed。

root: 来自古英语 cwysan（压），更早来源不确定；核心是两侧用力，由压水果引申出榨取钱财和挤进狭小空间。

sensesIntro.en: Squeeze means to press hard, to force liquid or money out, or to crowd into a space.
sensesIntro.cn: squeeze 指用力压、榨出液体或钱财，或挤进某个空间。

core.en: Pressure applied from two sides.
core.cn: 从两侧施加的压力。

branches.en: Two hands close on a lemon.
branches.cn: 两只手合拢压住柠檬。

branches.en: Coins drop from a tight fist.
branches.cn: 硬币从紧握的拳头里落下。

branches.en: A shoulder slips through a crowd.
branches.cn: 肩膀从人群中挤过去。

branches.en: Pressing fruit and pressing people both yield.
branches.cn: 压水果与压人，都会有所得。

branches.en: Tight money and tight space both squeeze.
branches.cn: 钱紧与地方窄，都让人受挤压。

intro.en: Squeeze forms verb parts, an agent noun, and adjectives.
intro.cn: squeeze 构成动词变化、施动名词和形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，是英语本族词。

items.exampleCN: 榨汁机就是一种挤压器。

items.example: The bottle is soft and squeezable.

definition_en: steady and not likely to change, firmly fixed, or a building for horses
core_image: 一架梯子稳稳地立在墙边
scene: 这架梯子很稳固。The ladder is stable.
sceneCN: 这里 stable 是「牢固的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这架梯子很稳固。

senses.title: Steady and lasting
senses.definition: not likely to change or fail
senses.definitionCN: 不易改变或失败
senses.example: The country has a stable economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家经济稳定。
senses.why: This abstract sense is the most common today.
senses.whyCN: 这个抽象义如今最常用。

senses.title: Firmly fixed
senses.definition: strongly built and not likely to move
senses.definitionCN: 建造结实、不易移动的
senses.example: The ladder is stable.
senses.exampleCN: 这架梯子很稳固。
senses.why: The physical sense supports the abstract one.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的「稳固」支撑了抽象含义。

senses.title: Building for horses
senses.definition: a building where horses are kept
senses.definitionCN: 关养马匹的建筑
senses.example: The horses were led into the stable.
senses.exampleCN: 马被牵进马厩。
senses.why: The noun sense comes from the same root, to stand.
senses.whyCN: 名词义同样源自「站立」的词根。

intro.en: Stable comes from Latin stabilis, standing firm, from stare, to stand.
intro.cn: stable 来自拉丁语 stabilis（站稳），词根 stare 意为站立。

items.en: Stabilis meant standing firm.
items.cn: stabilis 意为站稳的。

items.en: Estable meant firm or fixed.
items.cn: estable 意为坚固、固定。

items.en: Stable described firm things and places.
items.cn: stable 描述坚固的物体和场所。

items.en: The horse building sense grew from a standing place.
items.cn: 「马厩」义由「站立之处」发展而来。

items.en: The abstract sense now leads in use.
items.cn: 如今抽象义在使用中占主导。

note.en: Stable is compared with look-alike words and words for firmness.
note.cn: 把 stable 与形近词以及表示稳固的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small open shop or a stand

normalIntro.en: Stable means able to stand: a firm object, a steady state, or a horse's standing place.
normalIntro.cn: stable 意为「站得住」：牢固的物体、稳定的状态，或马站立之处。

normal.cn: 她需要一份稳定的工作。

abstract.en: What stands firm can bear weight.
abstract.cn: 站得稳的，才承得住重量。

abstract.en: A steady base makes a long climb safe.
abstract.cn: 稳固的底座让长途攀爬更安全。

abstract.en: Stillness is also a kind of strength.
abstract.cn: 静止不动也是一种力量。

examples.en: The country has a stable economy.
examples.cn: 这个国家经济稳定。

examples.en: The ladder is stable.
examples.cn: 这架梯子很稳固。

examples.en: The horses were led into the stable.
examples.cn: 马被牵进马厩。

dict_mnemonic.text: stable 是「稳定的、牢固的」，也指「马厩」；stay stable 是保持稳定，stable condition 是情况稳定；名词 stability 是稳定性。

root: 来自拉丁语 stabilis（站稳），词根 stare 意为站立；由「站得稳」引申出牢固、稳定，也指马匹站立之处「马厩」。

sensesIntro.en: Stable means steady, firmly fixed, or a building where horses are kept.
sensesIntro.cn: stable 指稳定的、牢固的，或关养马匹的建筑。

core.en: Standing firm and not easily moved.
core.cn: 站得稳，不易被移动。

branches.en: A graph line stays almost flat.
branches.cn: 曲线图上的线几乎保持水平。

branches.en: A ladder rests against a wall.
branches.cn: 梯子稳稳靠在墙上。

branches.en: Horses stand in separate stalls.
branches.cn: 马匹站在各自的隔间里。

branches.en: A firm base makes a steady life.
branches.cn: 牢固的根基带来安稳的生活。

branches.en: The horse house must also stand firm.
branches.cn: 马房本身也必须建得牢固。

intro.en: Stable forms comparisons, plurals, and a family of steady words.
intro.cn: stable 构成比较级、复数以及一组表示稳定的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is stabilis, from stare, to stand.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 stabilis，源自 stare（站立）。

items.example: The stables are behind the house.
This chair is stabler than that one.
It is the stablest table here.
